trial_court: Family Court, Matrimonial Case (Divorce) No. 560 of 2012
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1980 with two children born out of the wedlock. The respondent left the company of the petitioner in 1997 and began living in a hospital quarter. The petitioner made several attempts to repair the matrimonial bond but the respondent negated his company. The trial court dismissed the petition for divorce filed by the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: The standard of proof in civil cases is a preponderance of probabilities.
legal_principles.held: In civil cases this, normally, is the standard of proof to apply for finding whether the burden of proof is discharged.

legal_principles.principle: The standard of proof in matrimonial cases is a preponderance of probabilities, not beyond reasonable doubt.
legal_principles.held: Ruling out application of 'proof beyond reasonable doubt' in matrimonial cases, Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that the proof beyond reasonable doubt is proof by a higher standard which generally governs criminal trials or trials involving inquiry into issues of a quasi-criminal nature.

legal_principles.principle: The word 'satisfied' in Section 23 of the Hindu Marriage Act means 'satisfied on a preponderance of probabilities'.
legal_principles.held: Considering that proceedings under the Act are essentially of a civil nature, the word 'satisfied' must mean 'satisfied on a preponderance of probabilities' and not 'satisfied beyond a reasonable doubt'.

legal_principles.principle: The standard of proof in civil cases is not altered by the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Section 23 does not alter the standard of proof in civil cases.

outcome.final_order: The final court order allowed the appeal and granted a decree of divorce to the petitioner.
